title: The Manifestation of the Fated Registry
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was processing this earth-shaking truth, a strange ripple appeared in the void, and Mo Xiansheng's familiar residual soul phantom slowly materialized. The first words from his mouth sent a chill down Chen Ji's spine: "The registry from ten thousand years ago—do you think you were accidentally selected?"

text.content: The passage deep within the ruins was dark as ink, with ancient runes eroded by time covering both stone walls, emanating a dim cyan glow. Chen Ji walked slowly forward, his footsteps echoing in the vast corridor like a prelude to some ancient ritual. The Tianji Record Fragment in his arms grew slightly warm, a restlessness he had never experienced before, as if sensing something familiar. Ahead, a stone platform sealed for millennia stood quietly, with a visible crack running deep through its surface, from which a trace of golden light faintly emerged, creating a subtle resonance with the Tianji Record's fluctuations.

Chen Ji furrowed his brow but did not recklessly approach. He habitually surveyed his surroundings, confirming there were no ambushes before carefully approaching the platform. The fragment's temperature was rising rapidly, almost hot enough to burn through his robes. Chen Ji took a deep breath and reached out to touch the golden crack—at that instant, a vast tide of consciousness crashed into his Mental Sea. The Heavenly Eye, that ability which had never awakened on its own, activated by itself at this moment! Golden runes surged from the crack like a tidal wave, weaving into a massive scroll of names in the void.

The golden registry slowly unfurled, and Chen Ji saw countless names both familiar and foreign. Some names he had seen in ancient texts, figures who had shaken an era ten thousand years ago; other names bore detailed birth and death records and achievements, clearly a cross-millennium archive. Chen Ji's gaze swept rapidly across these names, his heartbeat accelerating—the span of this registry was far greater than he had imagined. Just then, a name suddenly caught his eye, freezing him solid as if thrown into an ice cavern.

"Chen Family's First Prophet—Chen Ji" That name hung quietly at the registry's core, with no birth or death records beside it, only a small line: "Selected by the Tianji Record, Candidate for the Ten Thousand Year Chess Game." Chen Ji felt a wave of intense dizziness wash over him. He was clearly a person of this era—how could he appear on a registry from ten thousand years ago? Unless... everything about him had been arranged from the start. The Heavenly Eye continued to trace backward, and at the registry's apex, a blurry yet supremely authoritative projection slowly formed, emanating a suffocating pressure—the will projection of the Heavenly Eye.

Chen Ji stared fixedly at that projection, his knuckles white from tension. From the projection, an ancient and authoritative voice rang in his mind: "Your name has entered the Book of Destiny, fated since ten thousand years ago. The Tianji Record was not given, but the beginning of shackles. You think you have arranged the chaos with your own strength, yet every move you make is on my chessboard." Chen Ji felt his blood boiling, anger and unwillingness intertwining into a raging fire. The Heavenly Eye, ten thousand years of scheming—all the opportunities he had gained were merely pieces in this grand game of chess?

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji, the only variable in ten thousand years of the Chen Family. However, variables are also within the calculations. The more complete the Tianji Record, the tighter the shackles. On the day you gather all the fragments, that is when fate shall be harvested. Hahaha..." That laughter was full of mockery and arrogance, as if watching an ant who believed itself to have escaped.

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, an unprecedented chill spreading from his spine through all four limbs and hundred bones. He suddenly understood something—the Tianji Record was not an inheritance, but a shackle; not an opportunity, but a trap. Every time he used the ability to foresee the future, the Heavenly Fate Value consumed was probably nourishing this so-called "Heavenly Will." Every step he had taken, every chess move he made, might be nothing more than a rehearsed drama in the eyes of the other party. The ten thousand year chess game had begun the moment he was born.

choice.prompt: Faced with the fate arrangement from ten thousand years ago, Chen Ji must make a choice—continue tracing the truth, or temporarily endure and face fate?

choices.description: Continue deeply tracing the complete truth behind the registry, risking possible triggers of the Heavenly Eye's trap, and uncover the full picture of the arrangement from ten thousand years ago.
choices.visible_cost: Consume 10 points of Heavenly Fate Value, possible exposure to the Heavenly Eye's surveillance
choices.visible_reward: Unlock deeper hidden information in the Tianji Record, obtain key flaws regarding the "Chess Game of Fate"
choices.risk_hint: High risk: The Heavenly Eye may take the opportunity to accelerate the tightening of the shackles

text.content: Chen Ji clenched his teeth tightly, an resolute light blazing in his eyes. He did not retreat; instead, he urged the Heavenly Eye to trace even deeper. Heavenly Fate Value flowed away like water, and the registry revealed more dust-laden information—he saw the names of every ancestor of the Chen Family through generations, with someone selected each generation, someone extinguished in despair each generation. And he himself was merely the newest piece in this lengthy game of chess.

Deepest within the registry, a line of deliberately hidden text finally emerged: "The method to break the game lies within the chess eye, only by self-sacrificing one piece can one turn the tables." Chen Ji shuddered all over, as if grasping something crucial. The Heavenly Eye thought it had trapped him死 within the game, yet it did not know that the true variable lay precisely herein.

choices.description: Calm down and face this cruel truth, temporarily sheathe your edge, and search for methods to break the shackles in secret rather than confront the Heavenly Will directly.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily abandon investigating the truth, possibly missing key information
choices.visible_reward: Maintain stable Heavenly Fate Value, gain "Endurance" status bonus, more deceptive when making future arrangements
choices.risk_hint: Low risk: But the truth may be learned by others first

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcefully suppressing the surging fury and unwillingness in his heart. He understood clearly—the Heavenly Eye, his current self was merely an ant trying to shake a tree. Anger would only expose more flaws; only endurance could find a narrow lifeline in desperation. He slowly withdrew the Heavenly Eye, allowing the registry's projection to gradually dissipate, his expression returning to calm.

"What a fine ten thousand year chess game." Chen Ji murmured to himself, the corner of his mouth actually curving into a cold smile. "Since you want me as a chess piece, then let me see if this chess game can truly be played out according to your script." He silently recorded everything he had seen today, deeply burying this hatred and vigilance. In time, he would certainly let this so-called Heavenly Will know—even ants can shake the heavens.

Just as Chen Ji's thoughts churned, the projection of that Heavenly Eye did not fully dissipate. A pair of intangible yet all-seeing eyes, faint and illusory in the void, fixed their gaze upon him. Chen Ji felt a bone-piercing chill, as if every pore of his body was laid bare. He knew this was a warning, a declaration of war—the Heavenly Eye conveying: Every thought of yours remains under my gaze.

Yet Chen Ji laughed. That smile carried a hint of madness, of recklessness, even of the satisfaction that comes from settling debts of gratitude or vengeance. He was not afraid of being seen through, for he never engaged in meaningless deeds. He was not afraid of being outmaneuvered, for true schemes never reveal themselves. Since Heaven wished to use him as a chess piece, then he would carve a blood-soaked path through this game. What mattered the list from ten thousand years ago? In today's world ten thousand years later, the chess player may yet become the one who shatters the board!

The temperature in the depths of the ruins seemed to plummet, Chen Ji's breath condensing into white mist. The projection of the Heavenly Eye finally faded completely, but the golden crack on the stone altar remained—a vicious wound revealing only the tip of a ten-thousand-year conspiracy. Chen Ji understood that today's vision was merely a fragment of truth, the complete truth hidden deeper within the fog. And he must grow stronger to be worthy of unveiling that veil.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji needed to decide his next move—investigate immediately, or leave first and plan later?

text.content: Chen Ji did not hesitate long. He had never been someone scared away by fear. While the Heavenly Eye's residual power had not yet fully faded, he strode deeper into the ruins. The runes on the stone walls grew denser the further he went, some even trembling faintly, as if sensing an intruder's presence. Suddenly, a faint Spiritual Light appeared ahead—that fluctuation... was Mo Xiansheng's aura!

choices.description: Temporarily retreat from the ruins, return to a safe location to organize today's information, and discuss strategy with Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul before deciding.
choices.visible_cost: Waste time, may miss the chance to discover new clues

text.content: Chen Ji ultimately chose to retreat temporarily. It was not that he was afraid, but that he deeply understood his excessive消耗 today. If he encountered danger again, he would struggle to cope. More importantly, he needed time to digest what he witnessed today, to discuss matters thoroughly with Mo Xiansheng. He turned to walk back the way he came, but paused briefly before the stone altar, firmly memorizing the location of that golden crack. This clue, he would never let slip.

Just as Chen Ji was about to step out of the stone chamber, a strange ripple suddenly appeared in the air. The ripple intensified, gradually forming a familiar figure—Mo Xiansheng. That remnant soul which had been sleeping on the first page of the Tianji Record now appeared before him in spectral form. Mo Xiansheng's features were even more blurred than before, as if a gust of wind could scatter him away, but those eyes remained sharp as blades as they gazed directly at Chen Ji.

dialogue.content: "What you just witnessed is merely the tip of the iceberg." Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted and wavered, yet every word rang clear. "The list from ten thousand years ago—do you think you were accidentally selected?" Chen Ji shuddered violently. Mo Xiansheng actually knew about that list's existence? Just as he was about to ask, Mo Xiansheng's phantom had already begun to fade.

text.content: "Wait!" Chen Ji instinctively reached out to grasp that remnant shadow, but touched only emptiness. Mo Xiansheng's form grew fainter and fainter, as if he had never existed at all, leaving only his final words echoing in the stone chamber: "The secrets of the Tianji Record run far deeper than you imagine... Some truths, once known, become a curse instead." When the voice faded, the stone chamber returned to dead silence. Only Chen Ji stood there, fists clenched, fingernails digging deep into his palms. How much did Mo Xiansheng truly know about the ten-thousand-year list? Chen Ji's doubts not only remained unresolved but piled higher and deeper.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, calming his emotions. He looked around, confirmed that Mo Xiansheng's remnant had completely dissipated, then slowly turned to walk toward the corridor's exit. The previous experience felt as unreal as a dream, but the faintly warm temperature of the Tianji Record Fragment reminded him that everything was real. He had been selected ten thousand years ago—the Tianji Record was not fortune but the beginning of shackles. Mo Xiansheng knew more yet refused to speak plainly... Each piece pressed against his heart like a massive stone. But Chen Ji had never been someone crushed by difficulties. On the contrary, the greater the pressure, the more his fighting spirit surged. A ten-thousand-year chess game? So what? Someday, he would flip this entire board upside down!
